source.title: Deep Learning Generalization, Extrapolation, and Over-parameterization

record.file_problem: None; the supplied text contains the full paper text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies generalization through convex-hull geometry and over-parameterization, using a different perspective and measurements from the listed versions. It does not directly test their train/test error claims.
record.gate_note: The paper's statements about fitting random labels and perfect training accuracy are cited background, not its own results. Its own results measure test samples' positions relative to training-set convex hulls, not test error or the listed version-specific outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study reports convex-hull geometry and discusses control of decision-boundary extensions. These results do not test any V1–V8 outcome. Random-label fitting is cited background; the paper supplies no width-versus-test-error results or other version-specific comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate as a statement of the author's argument: generalization should be understood through both interpolation and extrapolation, with over-parameterization and training regime shaping boundary extensions. The supplied paper asserts this mechanism without reporting quantitative generalization comparisons or presenting the claimed polynomial derivation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies convex-hull geometry and decision-boundary extrapolation rather than the listed memorization, width-versus-test-error, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, sharpness-gap, or example-removal experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that decision-boundary shapes outside the convex hull depend on the training regime.

fits_no_version.finding: Testing images lie outside the training-set convex hull in the examined pixel, wavelet, and learned representation spaces; random points in the same pixel domain lie farther away.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the examined image datasets and representations, held-out examples require extrapolation beyond the training-set convex hull.

fits_no_version.finding: The author argues that over-parameterization permits control of decision-boundary extensions and that the training regime determines their shape.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Over-parameterization and training regime jointly govern decision-boundary behavior outside the training-set convex hull.

record.peer_reviewed: preprint; abstract accepted and presented at the Workshop on Theory of Over-parameterized Machine Learning, April 2021
record.problems: The paper gives no quantitative test-error results for the geometric claims, and does not specify the neural-network training regimes, architecture details, or numerical results in the supplied discussion. Some geometry results are stated qualitatively.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe, including chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test-error behavior as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning and optimizer modifications.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce their penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error across dataset sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and comparisons with other measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: T2 is inappropriate because the different measurements address a different question from V1–V8. States of cannot_determine concern those versions; they do not deny the reported geometric observations.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance are cited from prior work, not tested here.
No width sweep on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10, no zero-training-error threshold comparison, and no test-error results.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected classifiers or test errors.
No optimizer comparison or held-out performance results.
No batch-size comparison or held-out performance results.
No dropout intervention or held-out error results.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap comparison.
No example-removal experiment or test-accuracy results.

rows.subject: MNIST testing images
rows.operation_detail: Measured testing images' positions relative to the training-set convex hull in pixel space.
rows.measure: Position relative to training-set convex hull
rows.value: All testing images are outside the corresponding training-set convex hull.
rows.note: This is a geometric result, not a test-error measurement.
rows.check: The geometric finding is reported, but convex-hull membership cannot establish any listed version.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 testing images
rows.operation_detail: Measured testing images' positions and distances relative to the training-set convex hull in pixel space.
rows.measure: Position and distance relative to training-set convex hull
rows.value: All testing images are outside the corresponding training-set convex hull; diameter is 13,621 and the farthest testing image is about 3,500 away (about 27% of the diameter).
rows.note: The paper states distances are measured by Frobenius norm in pixel space. This is not a test-error measurement.
rows.check: The distances and diameter match the text, including its approximate percentage; they do not measure any listed effect.

rows.subject: MNIST testing images
rows.operation_detail: Measured distances and shortest directions to the training-set convex hull after wavelet transformation.
rows.measure: Position and distance relative to training-set convex hull
rows.value: Testing samples remain outside the convex hull; distances resemble a normal distribution.
rows.note: The text reports the result for MNIST and CIFAR-10 together and does not separate values by dataset.
rows.check: Outside-hull membership after wavelet transformation is reported. The normal-like distance distribution is explicitly stated for selected wavelet coefficients, not separately for the full wavelet representation. Neither measures a listed effect.

rows.subject: standard ResNet model trained on the CIFAR-10 training set
rows.operation_detail: Measured testing samples' positions in the internal layer just before the last pooling layer.
rows.measure: Position relative to training-set convex hull
rows.value: Testing samples are outside the convex hull.
rows.locator: Section 2, Internal representation of images learned by deep learning
rows.note: The result concerns representation geometry, not test error.
rows.check: The representation geometry is reported, but supplies neither an architectural performance comparison nor another listed outcome.

rows.subject: standard ResNet model trained on the CIFAR-10 training set
rows.operation_detail: Measured testing samples' positions and distances after the last pooling layer.
rows.measure: Position and distance relative to training-set convex hull
rows.value: All testing samples are outside the convex hull; distances are significant compared to the size of the convex hull and resemble a normal distribution.
rows.locator: Section 2, Internal representation of images learned by deep learning
rows.note: No corresponding result is stated for the 10-dimensional output space.
rows.check: The 64-dimensional representation result matches the text, but cannot establish any listed effect.

rows.subject: random points in CIFAR-10's pixel-space domain
rows.operation_detail: Compared random points with training-set convex-hull geometry in the same high-dimensional domain.
rows.measure: Distance relative to training-set convex hull
rows.value: Random points are outside the convex hull and much farther away than testing data.
rows.locator: Section 2, Random data in high-dimensional space
rows.note: The paper attributes the difference to relationships between training and testing images, including similar training images closer to each testing image.
rows.check: Random input points are compared geometrically with natural images. This is not random-label training or a held-out accuracy comparison.

rows.subject: polynomial decision boundary using Legendre polynomials
rows.operation_detail: Studied the effect of over-parameterizing a polynomial decision boundary on control of its extensions outside the training-set convex hull.
rows.measure: Control over decision-boundary extensions outside the training-set convex hull
rows.value: The paper states over-parameterization is necessary to control the extensions; after over-parameterizing, a specific training regime is needed to obtain the desired boundary.
rows.locator: Section 3, Learning outside the convex hull of data: A polynomial decision boundary
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative conclusion, not numerical generalization results.
rows.check: Section 3 asserts a polynomial expressivity result without presenting its derivation or quantitative evaluation. It is not evidence that widening neural networks lowers test error.

rows.subject: neural network
rows.operation_detail: Compared under-parameterized and over-parameterized regimes in relation to training loss and decision-boundary behavior.
rows.value: The main struggle is minimizing training loss and finding the best shape of decision boundaries inside the convex hull.
rows.locator: Section 4, Effect of over-parameterization on the output of neural networks
rows.note: The text does not identify a specific architecture, dataset, optimizer, or test-error value.
rows.check: This is an unspecified qualitative account of the under-parameterized regime, not a reproducible comparison with measured training loss or test error. Preserve as an author assertion rather than a measured scaling result.

rows.subject: neural network
rows.operation_detail: Compared under-parameterized and over-parameterized regimes in relation to training loss and decision-boundary behavior.
rows.measure: Training loss and decision-boundary behavior inside and outside the convex hull
rows.value: Decision boundaries perfectly separate data inside the convex hull, but can have very different shapes outside it depending on training regime.
rows.locator: Section 4, Effect of over-parameterization on the output of neural networks
rows.note: The paper states over-parameterization gives control over behavior outside the convex hull through specific training regimes; it reports no test-error values.
rows.check: Section 4 gives a qualitative assertion without architecture, training-regime details, or measured outcomes. Perfect training separation and variable boundary extensions do not establish V2's declining test error.
